etymologies.heading: Etymology
paragraphs: From Middle English expedient, from Old French expedient, from Latin expediens (stem expedient-), present participle of expedire (“to bring forward, to dispatch, to expedite; impers. to be profitable, serviceable, advantageous, expedient”), from ex (“out”) + pēs (“foot, hoof”).
senses: Suitable to effect some desired end or the purpose intended.
Affording short-term benefit, often at the expense of the long-term.
A method or means for achieving a particular result, especially when direct or efficient; a resource.
